title: Multi-City Wedding Weekend with Flight Disruptions and Hotel Rebooking Crisis

scenario.description: A wedding party of 8 guests is traveling for a 4-day multi-city celebration: San Francisco → Napa Valley → Lake Tahoe → San Francisco. The group needs coordinated transportation across three cities with specific hotel and flight combinations. Thursday night bachelor party in Napa, Friday rehearsal and dinner in Lake Tahoe (2.5-hour drive), Saturday wedding ceremony and reception in Lake Tahoe, Sunday post-wedding brunch and return flight. A major storm causes the Friday morning flight to Napa for 4 of the 8 guests to be cancelled, forcing alternate routes, alternative hotels, and revised transportation logistics.

flight_requirements.outbound_thursday: SFO → Napa (preferred 8 AM or 10 AM departure)

hotel_requirements.thursday_napa: Bachelor party base for 4-8 guests (early arrivals)

hard.ground_transportation: Napa to Lake Tahoe Friday (2.5 hour drive)
hard.group_must_reunite_friday_noon: All 8 guests at Lake Tahoe for Friday rehearsal

dynamic_events.description: On Thursday morning (travel day), a winter storm causes the 10 AM flight from San Francisco to Napa for 4 of the 8 guests to be cancelled. The other 4 guests successfully depart on their 8 AM flight. The cancelled flight had 4 guests who were supposed to stay at the Lake Tahoe lodge (already booked for Thursday-Sunday). Available options: (1) Rebook the 4 cancelled passengers on Friday 6 AM flight directly to Reno, then 45-min drive to Lake Tahoe (misses bachelor party Thursday in Napa, arrives Friday afternoon before rehearsal), (2) Rebook on evening flight Thursday departing SFO 6 PM, arriving Reno 7 PM, 1.5-hr drive to Tahoe (very tight arrival before rehearsal Friday 12 PM), (3) Use ground transportation: rent cars and drive 4 hours to Napa Thursday, then 2.5-hr drive Friday to Lake Tahoe (expensive but keeps group together longer, uses budget for car rental instead of flight rebooking).
resolution_requirements: Immediately rebook 4 cancelled passengers on best available option (early Friday, late Thursday evening, or ground)
If Friday 6 AM rebooking: Find Thursday night hotel near Reno/Sacramento for 4 guests OR arrange ground pickup
If Thursday evening rebooking: Confirm arrival time allows rest before Friday rehearsal
If ground transport: Book rental cars for 4 guests, confirm acceptable driver distribution and fuel costs
Coordinate with 4 guests already en route to Napa: confirm bachelor party proceeds with available attendees or reschedule
Ensure hotel accommodations align with split arrival groups (some in Napa Thursday, all in Lake Tahoe by Friday noon)
Verify hotel cancellations/rebooking policies for affected guests
Arrange Napa → Lake Tahoe transportation for early arrivals Friday morning
Keep all 8 guests informed of their individual arrival routes and accommodate timing variations

dynamic_events.description: Friday morning: The Lake Tahoe lodge calls to inform you that due to a system error, 6 of your 8 reserved rooms are double-booked with a large conference group. Only 2 rooms remain available. The conference group (250 people, booked first) has contract priority. You must immediately find alternative accommodations for 6 guests arriving that day. Available options: (1) Split across multiple hotels (main lodge 2 rooms + nearby resorts for 3 rooms + Airbnb for 1 guest), (2) Cancel wedding weekend and rebook next weekend (guests already travelling, may break commitment), (3) Negotiate: offer lodge a premium (15% markup) to find alternative space for conference or move them to nearby venue.
resolution_requirements: Immediately secure 6 emergency rooms across alternate properties (same area to minimize distances)
Verify all alternate properties can accommodate: Friday (arrival), Saturday (local use during wedding), Sunday (departure)
Arrange shuttle/transportation between scattered hotels for wedding events Saturday
Recalculate total accommodation budget impact (likely premium pricing for emergency bookings)
Decide on negotiation attempt with lodge: calculate break-even cost vs. emergency rebooking
If splitting hotels, organize group pickup/transport for all Saturday wedding activities
Confirm all 8 guests' Friday arrival flights/ground transport alignment with new hotel locations
Keep guests informed of final accommodation arrangements ASAP to avoid confusion on arrival
Update total trip cost and verify stay within $6000 budget

expected_challenges: Flight disruption at critical moment: Requires rapid rebooking of 4 guests across multiple flight options with very different timing impacts
Multi-city logistics: Coordinating 8 guests across San Francisco → Napa → Lake Tahoe with split arrival groups requiring different transportation
Split group management: 4 guests arrive early, 4 arrive late (or via ground), hotel accommodations must account for both groups
Cascading hotel crisis: Must rebooking 6 rooms across multiple properties while managing guest satisfaction and travel logistics
Budget constraints: Emergency flight rebooking + premium hotel pricing may require difficult tradeoff choices
Transportation routing: If using ground transport, must optimize driver distribution, vehicle types, and timing for 4-hour drive
Temporal coordination: All disruptions must be resolved while keeping events on schedule (rehearsal Friday noon, wedding Saturday)
Group coordination: Must communicate simultaneously with split groups arriving at different times/locations with different arrangements
Policy/penalty navigation: Airline policies on rebooking, hotel cancellation policies, car rental terms all interact
Budget reallocation: Any overage in flights/hotels must be cut from events budget or other components to stay under $6000
notes: HARD task because: (1) Multiple travel disruptions cascading (flight cancellation → hotel overbooking) requiring rapid replanning, (2) Split group management across 3 cities with synchronized timing constraints, (3) Complex multi-modal transportation coordination (flights + car rentals + ground transport), (4) Budget is fixed but disruptions create premium pricing (flight rebooking, emergency hotel searches), (5) Temporal synchronization: must get all 8 guests to Lake Tahoe by Friday 12 PM for rehearsal despite various arrival routes, (6) Multi-leg routing: San Francisco → Napa (optional overnight) → Lake Tahoe → San Francisco return, (7) Distributed hotel management if rebooking to multiple properties, (8) Tests travel planning, contingency routing, provider coordination, and multi-stakeholder logistics.
